Maria: Hey team, noticed a recurring ~100-140ms tail spike on xlarge-8k around 22:40 UTC tied to a flurry of KV evictions on shard 7.
Kevin: Any repro or logs?
Maria: Pasted a tiny log window from the infra logs, you can see repeated evict+reinsert patterns.
Maria: ```
22:40:12.004 shard=7 evict start key_range=[0x3a..] reason=paging
22:40:12.005 shard=7 reinsert key=0x3a pos=tail
22:40:12.006 shard=7 evict key=0x3a
22:40:12.580 req=def456 latency=112ms stage=kv-miss
```
Srini: Which eviction policy is in use there? We swapped policies last week.
Kevin: That pool is running FIFO to reduce fragmentation for long-contexts.
Ben: FIFO can bounce hot entries if they get reinserted at tail while other threads still access them.
Olivia: Can you attach pprof/flame data for that span? I want to confirm whether allocator churn or CAS loops dominate.
Maria: Uploaded flame: https://infracloud/flame/shot/5678. Top frames are kv::evict_chain -> std::atomic::compare_exchange_weak -> allocator::free.
QA-Jen: I built a stress reproducer and ran it against staging: 
QA-Jen: ```bash
./kv_thrash --model xlarge-8k --policy=fifo --threads=48 --ctx=3072 --hotset=0.03 --time=90
```
QA-Jen: Result: median regressed +18ms, 99.9p jumped ~+95ms vs FIFO baseline. LRU baseline behaved much better on the same workload.
Srini: Hypothesis: with FIFO the reinsertion path forces entries to tail, and under high concurrency multiple threads can evict the same address repeatedly, causing allocator churn and possible pointer reuse races.
Ben: I found a code path where reinserts don't refresh any "seen" metadata, so a hot item reinserted goes to tail like a cold one.
Olivia: Could this cause correctness issues (use-after-free) or just perf? Any customer-visible corruption?
Maria: We saw two customer conversations where token duplication and weird repeated tokens happened; logs show the same pointer address being freed and then reassigned within microseconds.
Kevin: That's worrying. Short-term mitigation ideas?
Ben: Quick fix: add a lightweight generation counter on KV nodes to detect stale pointers on lookup. Also add a small exponential backoff before evicting the same key repeatedly.
QA-Jen: I pushed a staging canary with three changes:
- per-node 32-bit gen counter (atomic)
- reduce eviction high-watermark from 0.95 -> 0.86 for xlarge-8k
- per-key eviction backoff with a small randomized base
Maria: Staging stress results: 90s run -> 99.9p dropped from ~120ms to ~28ms, allocator free()/malloc() samples down ~7-10x.
Srini: Nice. Ben, paste the gen snippet?
Ben: ```c++
struct KVNode {
  std::atomic<uint32_t> gen{0};
  void mark_free() { gen.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed); }
  bool valid(uint32_t snapshot) const { return gen.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == snapshot; }
};
// On read: take snapshot, follow pointers, then verify valid(snapshot) before using pointers.
```
Kevin: Cost: ~4 bytes per entry, roughly 28MB on our largest shard. Acceptable vs safety.
Olivia: Agreed. Also tune per-model watermarks: long-context models need more headroom to avoid mass paging.
Maria: Rollback plan: if canary doesn't degrade we'll flip affected prod pool back to LRU by 23:30 UTC and keep gen+backoff in staging a bit longer. Add perf alert on allocator churn > 3x baseline.
Infra-bot: deploy rwi-kv/2026.3.15-evict-mitigation -> staging in 1m :rocket:
QA-Jen: PR #1497 includes unit tests, perf harness, and flame capture scripts.
Srini: Follow-ups for the write-up:
- root cause: FIFO reinsertion semantics + concurrency leading to reevict loops and allocator churn
- short-term: gen counter + backoff + lower watermark
- medium-term: hybrid policy (FIFO placement + LRU promotion on repeat hits), and smarter batching to reduce parallel eviction pressure
- long-run: validate memory growth with gen counter on 100k token soaks to ensure no leak masked by gen
Maria: I'll run a 6h soak in staging with the canary and post numbers tomorrow. Tagging Kevin/Ben/Olivia for visibility :eyes:
Kevin: Thanks, please also add a metric for repeated-evict-per-key so we can alert if a key is being evicted > N times in T window.
Ben: Good call. Also consider making reinsert update an "age" hint so we avoid demoting truly hot items to tail.
Olivia: I can sketch a hybrid design doc if you want; it would combine FIFO for initial allocation with a low-overhead LRU hint counter to promote items seen twice within window.
Maria: Sounds good. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Kevin: If staging holds, plan a staged prod rollout with LRU fallback and tight monitoring.
Maria: Any other comments?
Ben: Just a note: allocator-level tuning (slab reuse) helped in one experiment but made fragmentation worse elsewhere, so be careful.
Maria: Noted. I'll include that in the follow-up.
Infra-bot: canary health ok, flame snapshots captured, logs archived.
